ref: incremental-verifier prompt, Testing Protocol step 2 (golden suite) + Build Environment (Bash timeout cap 600000 ms)
what: The protocol prescribes ONE command -- eval/eval_test_runner.sh eval/golden_tests/{op}/ <results_dir> -- for the golden suite. For this op that selection collects 121438 cells, and the runner ALWAYS does a collect+precompile warm pass over the WHOLE selection before running anything: ~10 min of collect, 15620 unique programs compiled, then 30+ min pinned single-threaded on the main thread having produced zero output. It cannot finish inside the 10-minute Bash ceiling, and because the warm pass emits nothing until it completes there is no progress signal to judge by -- I could not tell 'still working' from 'wedged'. I burned ~75 min on one aborted invocation before concluding it had to be sharded, and the SIGTERM left the device dirty. The implementer logged the same wall from THEIR prompt, so this is the second agent to pay it on this op.
suggest: In the Testing Protocol, state that a whole-directory golden run may not fit one invocation, and give the escape hatch inline: eval_test_runner.sh forwards extra pytest args verbatim, so shard with -k <shape ids> plus --no-precompile, and merge the per-shard sidecars before calling eval.verify_supported (test_results.json is a LIST of records keyed by nodeid; test_axes/extras/groups.json are dicts keyed by nodeid). Overlapping -k selectors are safe because merging by nodeid de-duplicates. This run committed a reusable harness -- scripts/verifier_golden_shards.sh + scripts/verifier_merge_golden_shards.py -- so pointing at it, or just at the pattern, would save the next agent the same 75 minutes.

ref: .claude/references/ (no doc covers it) + ttnn/ttnn/operations/examples/master.md + incremental-verifier prompt, 'Perf refinements' (every lever is gated on a measured device-ns A/B)
what: A kernel-source A/B can leave a POISONED JIT artifact that survives clearing the cache dir, and nothing warns about it. I flipped one template arg in the compute kernel (ReduceFp32Mode::Fast -> Accurate), measured, then reverted the file to byte-identical-with-HEAD. The REVERTED source kept being served the EXPERIMENT's binary: test_rms_norm_ttnn_debug.py went 2/19 red with non-finite output on exactly the config the experiment had compiled (float32 + math_approx_mode=True + eps=1e-12), while the same cells passed in the golden suite (which pins math_approx_mode=False) and in the precision baseline (which uses a different epsilon). `rm -rf built` did NOT clear it even though TT_METAL_CACHE=<repo>/built -- this env also sets TT_METAL_CCACHE_KERNEL_SUPPORT=1 and TT_METAL_JIT_SERVER_ENDPOINT, and the stale artifact came back from one of those. Only a fresh TT_METAL_CACHE=<tmpdir>, or --no-jit-server, gave correct results. I spent ~30 min treating it as a real op correctness bug -- ran five characterisation probes, sweeping width/epsilon/seed/approx-mode -- and came within a step of filing a false severity=bug correctness finding against a shipped op that was in fact fine.
suggest: Add a short 'measuring a kernel variant' note to the perf reference (master.md preamble or a .claude/references entry) and to the verifier/perf prompts: when you A/B a KERNEL SOURCE, give each variant its own TT_METAL_CACHE=<fresh tmp dir> or pass --no-jit-server; clearing $TT_METAL_CACHE is NOT sufficient when a JIT server or ccache is configured. Note the failure signature explicitly, because it is silent and looks exactly like an op bug: tests that passed before the A/B fail afterwards on the specific config the experiment compiled, while the same configuration passes under a different epsilon / dtype / compute-config (each of which is a different build key and so a different, uncontaminated artifact). This bites every perf refinement, since every one of them is a kernel A/B.
